 Date of Institution : 18.04.2023  Date of Reserving Order : 24.05.2024  Date of Order : 28.05.2024 REVISION PETITION U/s. 397 Cr. P.C. FOR SETTING ASIDE THE IMPUGNED ORDER DATED 02.06.2022 OF LD. MM-04 WEST IN FIR No. 69-2020 PS MOTI NAGAR DIRECTING SUMMONING OF ACCUSED PERSONS AUDHESH KUMAR PANDEY, RAVINDER DHIMAN AND RAHUL JAIN QUA OFFENCES U/S 304A/34 IPC.
ORDER:
1. Vide this common order, I shall dispose off three revision CR No. 2192023 Audhesh Kumar Pandey Vs State CR No. 2202023 Ravinder Dhiman Vs State petitions detailed above as they are arising out of the same order.
2. Revisionists Audhesh Kumar Pandey, Ravinder Dhiman and Rahul Jain have filed three separate revision petitions challenging the impugned order dated 02.06.2022 whereby Ld. MM-04, West has summoned them for being tried for offence u/s 304A/34 IPC in case FIR No. 69-2020 PS Moti Nagar.
3. Revisionists are accused no. 1, 2 and 3 before Ld. Trial Court. One other accused namely Ajeet Singh Shekhawat was also chargesheeted and summoned in the abovementioned FIR, however, he has not challenged the impugned order before any court. State has been impleaded as Respondents Rahul Jain vs State on 28 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141937491/
2 in the present revision petitions. Since, the matter was pertaining to Section 304A IPC, vide order dated 18.04.2023, directions were also issued for summoning of the complainant. The complainant had appeared through his counsel and contested the present revision petitions. For the sake of convenience, parties shall be referred to by their nomenclature before Ld. Trial Court. 
4. Arguments on the revision petitions have been heard. Record carefully perused. 
BRIEF FACTS:
5. Brief facts of the case necessary for disposal of the present revision petitions are that on 06.06.2019, an information was received at PS Moti Nagar vide DD No. 9A regarding a person being brought dead at Gangaram Hospital vide MLC No. 4051/2019. The deceased was identified and it was informed that he had fallen into the shaft of M-tower of DLF Capital Greens, Shivaji Marg, Moti Nagar, Delhi from a height of about 35-40 feet. At that time, no one suspected any foul play. 
Accordingly, proceedings u/s 174 CrPC were conducted. During the CR No. 2192023 Audhesh Kumar Pandey Vs State CR No. 2202023 Ravinder Dhiman Vs State proceedings, the place of incident was inspected by the crime team and it was found that the iron cover of the shaft of M-tower of DLF Capital Greens was not fastened with the wall of the building or side railings from where the deceased had fallen. The photographs of the place of the incident were taken. Post mortem of the dead body was conducted and the dead body was handed over to the relatives of the deceased. 
6. In the meanwhile, an application u/s 156 (3) CrPC was filed by the wife of the deceased through her attorney in the concerned court alleging contributory negligence of M/s DLF and M/s JLL being the construction company and the maintenance company of the DLF towers in the accident that had occurred on 06.06.2019 resulting in demise of her husband. It was alleged that due to their negligence to ensure proper safety to the occupants and visitors, the accident had taken place which has resulted in demise of deceased Sandeep. Accordingly, necessary directions were sought for initiating criminal action against them. 
7. Vide order dated 10.01.2020, Ld. Trial Court allowed the application u/s 156(3) CrPC and directed police investigation into the matter. Thereafter, FIR No. 69/2020 u/s 304A IPC was registered on 28.01.2020 and IO undertook the investigation. 
8. During investigation, the place of incident was again got inspected and it was found that the iron cover of the shaft of M- tower which was earlier not fastened with the wall was now found fastened with the wall by welding and with the help of screws. It was also found that the place of incident was adjoining to the fire/emergency exit gate but it was kept open in routine. It was also found that there was no warning or danger sign board CR No. 2192023 Audhesh Kumar Pandey Vs State CR No.
2202023 Ravinder Dhiman Vs State for the visitors not to visit the area where the accident had occurred. Notices were issued to DLF u/s 91 CrPC i.e. the construction company of the project. They gave their written reply to the effect that construction of the last phase of the project was completed in October, 2016. The occupation cum completion certificate of the last phase was granted by the competent authority on 05.04.2017. The Resident Association had outsourced the entire Rahul Jain vs State on 28 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141937491/
3 maintenance/operations including safety and security of the common areas and the facilities to the maintenance company M/s JLL having technical expertise in the matter. Subsequent to the said reply, notice u/s 91 CrPC was also issued to Resident Welfare Association who admitted the engagement of the M/s JLL vide an Integrated Asset and Facility Management Services Agreement dated 01.01.2019. The copy of the agreement was furnished wherein the role and responsibility of JLL for maintenance, upkeeping and security of the said premises was elaborated. The agreement also had Clause 8 as per which JLL shall solely be responsible or liable for all consequences of any accident, mishap or untoward accident resulting in any injuries or loss of life to any person at the Project site. The particulars of Directors of JLL were obtained from ROC and it was found that accused Audhesh Kumar Pandey, Ravinder Dhiman and Rahul Jain were the Directors of the company at the time of the incident and were responsible for day to day maintenance and security/safety of the complex where the accident had taken place. All three of them along with Ajeet Singh Shekhawat, who was the Project Manager of the complex were made to join the investigation. 
9. After completion of investigation, chargesheet u/s 304A/34 CR No. 2192023 Audhesh Kumar Pandey Vs State CR No. 2202023 Ravinder Dhiman Vs State IPC were filed against all the four accused persons on 02.06.2022. 
10. Vide impugned order dated 02.06.2022, Ld. Trial Court took cognizance of the offences and directed issuance of summons to all the accused persons. It is this order summoning the Revisionists/ accused no. 1, 2 and 3 which is under challenge in these revision petitions. 
GROUNDS FOR REVISION:
11. It is submitted by Ld. Counsel for the Revisionists that they have been wrongly summoned as accused persons in the present case. 
12. Accused Audhesh Kumar Pandey is the Property Asset Management Head (Commercial) of M/s JLL and is based in the Corporate office of the company at Gurgaon. His job profile includes preparing the strategy and planning of the business, working with the regional leadership in getting the plans executed, maintaining the financial discipline, supervising client invoicing and payment through the service partners and working with the respective regional leads to facilitate their functioning and resolving their issues. 
13. Accused Ravinder Dhiman is the Property Asset Management, National Head, Business Support (Residential). He is based in Mumbai. His job profile includes technology development and implementation, procurement, EOS (Engineering Operations and Solution) Training System and Processes. With effect from 01.04.2021, his job profile has changed to that of Business P&L, overall operations of residential assets and development operations. 
14. Accused Rahul Jain is working as Finance Head of M/s CR No. 2192023 Audhesh Kumar Pandey Vs State CR No. 2202023 Ravinder Dhiman Vs State JLL and is based in Bengalaru. His job profile is to supervise corporate and client finance schemes including budgeting, financials,
closing, reporting, managing working capital, cash flow, financial transactions, streamlining Rahul Jain vs State on 28 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141937491/
4 accounts, MIS reports, developing plans for financial growth and coordinating financial audits. It is submitted that none of these three revisionists are involved in day to day operations and management of any particular premises/facility and their role is limited to strategic management and planning of business. At the time of unfortunate accident, all three of them were in their respective offices at Gurgaon, Mumbai and Bengalaru. 
15. It is submitted that as per the investigation conducted by the Investigating Officer, the unfortunate accident had transpired on account of own negligence of the deceased and that is the reason why no FIR was registered in the matter. Even otherwise, no case is made out against the revisionists as they had no active role in the alleged accident that had taken place on 06.06.2019 resulting in demise of the deceased. The chargesheet does not disclose any offence or active involvement of any of the revisionists with any criminal intent in relation to the unfortunate incident. They have been chargesheeted merely because of the reason that they were Directors of M/s JLL maintenance company at the relevant time. Bare persual of the chargesheet makes it abundantly clear that there is no specific allegation of negligence with criminal intent qua the revisionists nor any active role of any of them has come on record during the investigation. No nexus between the unfortunate incident and the revisionists has been established during the investigation. Accordingly, the revisionists herein are not liable for prosecution CR No. 2192023 Audhesh Kumar Pandey Vs State CR No. 2202023 Ravinder Dhiman Vs State and should not have been summoned by Ld. Trial Court. In addition to this, there is no material on record which shows or discloses existence of any common intention between the revisionists and thus, Section 34 IPC cannot be attracted in the matter. There is no incriminating evidence against any of the revisionists but Ld. Trial court had proceeded to summon them as accused without due application of mind. The impugned order is clearly illegal and erroneous and needs to be set aside as it has been passed in a mechanical manner without due consideration to the facts brought on record during investigation. It is a fundamental principle of criminal law that a person cannot be put to trial without any allegation of prima facie nature being made out against him. The passing of impugned order thereby summoning the revisionists without any incriminating evidence against them has caused grave prejudice to them and miscarriage of justice. Thus, the impugned order needs to be set aside. This is more so as the company M/s JLL has not been impleaded as an accused and the revisionists cannot be made vicariously liable merely on account of being a Director of JLL. Accordingly, setting aside of the impugned order is prayed. 
16. Ld. Counsel for the revisionists has relied upon the following decisions of the superior courts in support of his arguments:
(i) Sunil Bharti Mittal V. CBI (2015) 4 SCC 609.
(ii) Shiv Kumar Jatia v. State of NCT of Delhi (2019) 17 SCC 193. 
(iii) Ravindranatha Bajpe v. Mangalore SEZ 2021 SCC Online SC 806. 
Rahul Jain vs State on 28 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141937491/ 
5 (iv) Pepsi Foods Ltd. v. Special Judicial Magistrate (1998) 5 CR No. 2192023 Audhesh Kumar Pandey Vs State CR No. 2202023 Ravinder Dhiman Vs State SCC 749. 
(v) Maksud Saiyed V. State of Gujarat (2008) 5 SCC 668. 
(vi) Chunduru Siva Ram Krishna V. Paddi Ravindra Babu (2009) 11 SCC 203. 
(vii) GHCL Employees Stock Option Trust V. India Infoline Ltd. (2013) 4 SCC 505. 
(viii) Benita Sharma V. Anil Kumar Sharma 2022 SCC Online Del 4353. 
(ix) Kabita Ghosh V. CBI 2022 SCC Online DEL 1043. 
(x) Guljeet Singh Kochar V. State 2005 SCC Online Del 706. ARGUMENTS OF RESPONDENTS:
17. Per contra, the revision petition has been vehementally opposed on behalf of the State as well as Ld. Counsel for complainant. It is submitted that the impugned order is a well reasoned order based on the material available on record. There is no infirmity or illegality in the impugned order and no interference is required by this court. 
18. It is submitted on behalf of the complainant that the photographs of the buildings taken at the time of incident which are available on record clearly show that there was a criminal negligence in securing the shaft at the place where the incident had occurred. There were about 100 sheets covering the shaft area which were duly welded and screwed to avoid any untoward incident. 
However, the shaft in question where the incident had occurred was unsecured, neither it was welded nor secured by using screws. There is ample evidence on record in the form of replies of DLF and RWA that it was the maintenance company which was responsible for the maintenance and upkeep of the entire complex including the stilts, basement, fire exits as well as CR No. 2192023 Audhesh Kumar Pandey Vs State CR No. 2202023 Ravinder Dhiman Vs State the shaft area. 
Accordingly, the prime responsibility for any untoward incident was that of maintenance company JLL. Chargesheet also shows that after registration of FIR, when the place of incident was again visited, the iron sheets were affixed and the area was secured by JLL.
19. The impugned order is completely a legal order and within the jurisdiction of Ld. MM. There is no illegality or infirmity in the same as simply the cognizance has been taken and the summons have been issued to chargesheeted accused persons. Revisional jurisdiction is limited in nature and impugned order cannot be set aside merely because another view is possible. It has to be shown that an order is illegal, infirm, perverse or beyond the jurisdiction of Ld. Trial Court before it can be interfered with. However, in this case, there is no such illegality or infirmity in the impugned order . 
As regards the grounds taken in the present revision petition, the same can be considered at the stage of arguments on charge. Moreover, the responsibilities of the revisionist as Directors of M/s JLL can only be established at the stage of evidence. 
Rahul Jain vs State on 28 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141937491/
6 20. In these circumstances, it is submitted that the present revision petitions are not maintainable and deserve to be dismissed. 
21. It is also submitted that the decision in Sunil Bharti's case (supra) is distinguishable on facts as in that case, the accused persons not chargesheeted were summoned by the court whereas in the present case, the revisionists/accused persons have been duly chargesheeted. Similarly, the decision in Pepsi Food's case (supra) is not applicable to the facts of the present case as it was an order passed in a quashing petition filed u/s 482 CrPC while CR No. 2192023 Audhesh Kumar Pandey Vs State CR No. 2202023 Ravinder Dhiman Vs State in the present case, the impugned order has been challenged in a revision petition and accordingly, the scope of revisional jurisdiction has to be kept in mind.
FINDINGS:
22. I have heard the submissions made and carefully perused the record as well as citations relied upon by the parties. 
23. It is held by the Apex Court in Kishan Lal Vs. Dharmender Bafna & Anr. Crl. No. 1283/2009 that a revisional court should not interfere with the discretionary jurisdiction exercised by Ld. Magistrate unless a jurisdictional error or an error of law is noticed. 
24. In the present case, the Revisionists have been summoned as accused to be tried for offence u/s 304A IPC. Sec. 304A IPC provides punishment for causing death by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide. While rashness is acting in the hope that no mischievous consequences will ensue, though aware of the likelihood of such consequences; negligence is acting without the awareness that harmful or mischievous consequences will follow, but in circumstances which show that had the actor exercised caution incumbent upon him, he would have had awareness of the consequences of his act. What is or not negligent involves a consideration of that which a reasonable man would or not would not have done in the circumstances. This does not invariably rule out of consideration of subjective factors such as a person's knowledge, physical condition or age. 
25. In order to make out a case u/s 304A IPC against an accused, it is required to show that it was the accused who did some act which was rash or negligent; that act resulted in death CR No. 219 2023 Audhesh Kumar Pandey Vs State CR No. 2202023 Ravinder Dhiman Vs State of a person;
the death was the direct result of rashness or negligence; and the said rash and negligent act did not amount to culpable homicide. Thus, the prime requirement for invoking Section 304A against an accused is to show that it was he who had committed rash and negligent act. Connecting the accused with the rash and negligent act is of vital importance in a case u/s 304A IPC.
26. Coming to the facts of the present case, although, there is ample evidence on record to show that the responsibility of maintenance at the place of incident was of the maintenance company M/s JLL. 
There is also prima facie evidence to show that the incident had occurred due to the breach of duty of M/s JLL in maintaining the safety and security of the place of incident to avoid any untoward Rahul Jain vs State on 28 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141937491/
7 incident. Since, the breach of duty of M/s JLL in maintaining the site has resulted in demise of a person, the same can also be characterised as gross negligence as required for attracting the offence u/s 304A IPC. However, it is a fact that the company M/s JLL has not been impleaded as an accused in the present case. The revisionists herein are chargesheeted as accused persons merely on account of their designation as Directors in the maintenance company M/s JLL. A bare perusal of the chargesheet clearly show that the only reason given for impleading the revisionists herein as accused persons in the present FIR is the fact that they were Directors of JLL. No overt or covert act of negligence has been attributed to them in the entire chargesheet. The investigation has not revealed their presence at the place of incident at the time of incident. It is also amply clear from the chargesheet that Revisionist Audhesh Kumar Pandey is based in Gurgaon, revisionist Ravinder Kumar CR No. 2192023 Audhesh Kumar Pandey Vs State CR No. 2202023 Ravinder Dhiman Vs State Dhiman is based in Mumbai while Revisionist Rahul Jain is based in Bengalaru. It is not the case of the IO that any of these revisionists had visited and personally checked safety and security of the place of incident. No vicarious liability in such circumstances is recognised in criminal law. This is more so in the present case as the maintenance company itself (JLL) has not been made an accused. Perusal of the entire charge-sheet clearly shows that there is no evidence on record to show any rash or negligent act at the hands of the revisionists herein which is sufficient to put them to trial in the present FIR. Moreover, attracting the provision u/s 34 IPC in the facts and circumstances of the case is beyond the scope of Section 34 IPC itself. No common intention to commit a rash and negligent act resulting in the reported accident can be imputed on the revisionists. Accordingly, it is not proper to prosecute the revisionists herein by attracting Section 34 IPC against them. It is a settled law that summoning of an accused is a serious order which entails a number of legal consequences and same should not be passed in a casual manner. The Court has to be prima facie convinced that there is sufficient incriminating material for proceeding against an accused before summoning him for trial. This is all in the cases whether an accused has been chargesheeted or not chargesheeted by the IO. 
27. In view of the reasons given above and considering the material available on record, I am of the opinion that impugned order dated 02.06.2022 suffers from infirmity and illegality as it has directed summoning of the revisionists herein without appreciating the evidence that has been collected by the IO during the investigation against them. Ld. Trial Court has CR No. 2192023 Audhesh Kumar Pandey Vs State CR No. 2202023 Ravinder Dhiman Vs State committed error of law by summoning the accused no. 1, 2 and 3 i.e. Revisionists herein merely because they have been chargesheeted by the IO and without going through the evidence brought on record during investigation. Accordingly, the present revision petitions are allowed and the impugned order dated 02.06.2022 qua the summoning of accused Audhesh Kumar Pandey, Ravinder Kumar Dhiman and Rahul Jain i.e. the revisionists herein is set aside. 
28. Nothing expressed herein shall tantamount to an expression of opinion on the merits of the case. 
29. TCR be sent back along with a copy of this order. 
30. Revision files be consigned to Record Room after completion of all legal formalities.

annotations.text: 24. In the present case, the Revisionists have been summoned as accused to be tried for offence u/s 304A IPC.
Sec. 304A IPC provides punishment for causing death by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide.

While rashness is acting in the hope that no mischievous consequences will ensue, though aware of the likelihood of such consequences; negligence is acting without the awareness that harmful or mischievous consequences will follow, but in circumstances which show that had the actor exercised caution incumbent upon him, he would have had awareness of the consequences of his act.
What is or not negligent involves a consideration of that which a reasonable man would or not would not have done in the circumstances.
This does not invariably rule out of consideration of subjective factors such as a person's knowledge, physical condition or age.

25. In order to make out a case u/s 304A IPC against an accused, it is required to show that it was the accused who did some act which was rash or negligent; that act resulted in death CR No. 219 2023 Audhesh Kumar Pandey Vs State CR No. 2202023 Ravinder Dhiman Vs State of a person;
the death was the direct result of rashness or negligence; and the said rash and negligent act did not amount to culpable homicide.

There is also prima facie evidence to show that the incident had occurred due to the breach of duty of M/s JLL in maintaining the safety and security of the place of incident to avoid any untoward Rahul Jain vs State on 28 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141937491/

However, it is a fact that the company M/s JLL has not been impleaded as an accused in the present case.
The revisionists herein are chargesheeted as accused persons merely on account of their designation as Directors in the maintenance company M/s JLL.
A bare perusal of the chargesheet clearly show that the only reason given for impleading the revisionists herein as accused persons in the present FIR is the fact that they were Directors of JLL.
No overt or covert act of negligence has been attributed to them in the entire chargesheet.
The investigation has not revealed their presence at the place of incident at the time of incident.

annotations.text: It is not the case of the IO that any of these revisionists had visited and personally checked safety and security of the place of incident.
No vicarious liability in such circumstances is recognised in criminal law.
This is more so in the present case as the maintenance company itself (JLL) has not been made an accused.

Perusal of the entire charge-sheet clearly shows that there is no evidence on record to show any rash or negligent act at the hands of the revisionists herein which is sufficient to put them to trial in the present FIR.
Moreover, attracting the provision u/s 34 IPC in the facts and circumstances of the case is beyond the scope of Section 34 IPC itself.
No common intention to commit a rash and negligent act resulting in the reported accident can be imputed on the revisionists.
Accordingly, it is not proper to prosecute the revisionists herein by attracting Section 34 IPC against them.
It is a settled law that summoning of an accused is a serious order which entails a number of legal consequences and same should not be passed in a casual manner.
The Court has to be prima facie convinced that there is sufficient incriminating material for proceeding against an accused before summoning him for trial.
This is all in the cases whether an accused has been chargesheeted or not chargesheeted by the IO.

27. While rashness is acting in the hope that no mischievous consequences will ensue, though aware of the likelihood of such consequences; negligence is acting without the awareness that harmful or mischievous consequences will follow, but in circumstances which show that had the actor exercised caution incumbent upon him, he would have had awareness of the consequences of his act.
What is or not negligent involves a consideration of that which a reasonable man would or not would not have done in the circumstances.

25. In order to make out a case u/s 304A IPC against an accused, it is required to show that it was the accused who did some act which was rash or negligent; that act resulted in death CR No. 219 2023 Audhesh Kumar Pandey Vs State CR No. 2202023 Ravinder Dhiman Vs State of a person;
the death was the direct result of rashness or negligence; and the said rash and negligent act did not amount to culpable homicide.
Thus, the prime requirement for invoking Section 304A against an accused is to show that it was he who had committed rash and negligent act.
Since, the breach of duty of M/s JLL in maintaining the site has resulted in demise of a person, the same can also be characterised as gross negligence as required for attracting the offence u/s 304A IPC.
No vicarious liability in such circumstances is recognised in criminal law.
Perusal of the entire charge-sheet clearly shows that there is no evidence on record to show any rash or negligent act at the hands of the revisionists herein which is sufficient to put them to trial in the present FIR.
Moreover, attracting the provision u/s 34 IPC in the facts and circumstances of the case is beyond the scope of Section 34 IPC itself.
No common intention to commit a rash and negligent act resulting in the reported accident can be imputed on the revisionists.
Accordingly, it is not proper to prosecute the revisionists herein by attracting Section 34 IPC against them.
It is a settled law that summoning of an accused is a serious order which entails a number of legal consequences and same should not be passed in a casual manner.
The Court has to be prima facie convinced that there is sufficient incriminating material for proceeding against an accused before summoning him for trial.

Accordingly, the present revision petitions are allowed and the impugned order dated 02.06.2022 qua the summoning of accused Audhesh Kumar Pandey, Ravinder Kumar Dhiman and Rahul Jain i.e. the revisionists herein is set aside.
